gen_risks.description: Severe floods could trigger a sharp rise in non‑performing loans and erode capital adequacy of micro‑finance banks, limiting their lending capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate the Contingent Liquidity Facility promptly, maintain capital buffers, and monitor NPL trends to provide early liquidity support.
gen_risks.evidence: Floods 2022 caused NPLs to surge 25.7% and CAR to fall from 14.9% to 11.7%, impairing sector lending.

gen_risks.description: The Climate Risk Fund may be under‑capitalised to meet funding needs of large or extreme flood events.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct annual financial modelling, secure additional capital or insurance back‑stop, and obtain Board approval for any extra funding.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF capitalised at US$125 m; expansion of coverage to additional climate risks would require additional capital subject to approval.

gen_risks.description: Delays in activating CRF triggers due to slow government emergency declarations or data gaps could postpone liquidity disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define pre‑agreed quantitative thresholds, automate data feeds from third‑party providers, and establish clear SOPs for trigger verification.
gen_risks.evidence: Triggers require government emergency declaration or portfolio impact thresholds, with data supplied by third‑party service providers.

gen_risks.description: Governance conflicts or mismanagement within the Trust structure could compromise CRF operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an Oversight Committee, conduct independent internal and external audits, and enforce fiduciary safeguards in the Trust Deed.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF established as a Trust owned by GoP, managed by SBP as Trustee; Oversight and Working Committees will govern operations.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with legal covenants (e.g., unauthorized amendment of the Trust Deed) could lead to project suspension.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform regular legal compliance reviews, obtain prior written consent for any amendment, and maintain legal counsel oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require Trust Deed not be amended without Association consent and specify obligations for SBP.

gen_risks.description: Risk modelling currently excludes droughts, extreme heat and other hazards, potentially under‑estimating sector exposure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Expand modelling to incorporate additional climate hazards and update trigger parameters accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Preliminary risk modelling limited to floods; future work will consider extreme heat and droughts.

gen_risks.description: Increased agritech financing may lead to higher use of fertilizers and pesticides, causing localized environmental degradation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate environmental safeguards, promote integrated pest management, and monitor chemical usage in loan‑linked agritech projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Cumulative impacts may increase fertilizer, pesticide use and air/soil pollution in loan‑clustered areas.

gen_risks.description: Women borrowers may receive less than the targeted share of CRF liquidity, limiting gender‑inclusive resilience gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce the 55% women beneficiary target, impose higher borrowing costs for non‑compliance, and provide gender‑sensitive training for loan officers.
gen_risks.evidence: Project aims for at least 55% women beneficiaries; higher borrowing cost if deviation occurs.

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability could reduce borrowers’ repayment capacity, increasing default risk after floods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design flexible loan terms, monitor macro indicators, and adjust liquidity provision to support stressed borrowers.
gen_risks.evidence: Macro‑economic crisis since 2019 amplified flood impacts, leading to higher NPLs and reduced sector growth.

gen_risks.description: Failure to secure the parametric insurance back‑stop would leave the CRF under‑funded for extreme events.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct annual financial and technical reviews of the insurance product, maintain a reserve fund, and explore alternative reinsurance options.
gen_risks.evidence: Insurance back‑stop purchase decided annually; premium funded by GSFF grant and CRF investment income.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing the CRF Trust and capitalising it could postpone project start‑up and liquidity provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear milestones for Trust registration, front‑load funding to pooled accounts, and monitor progress with monthly reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: Funds will be front‑loaded to pooled account for CRF capitalization; trust structure requires registration.

gen_risks.description: Poor quality or untimely MIS data may impair monitoring, trigger decisions and overall project performance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen MIS infrastructure, conduct regular data quality audits, and provide capacity‑building for SBP staff.
gen_risks.evidence: SBP responsible for MIS; data sources include bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient citizen engagement could result in loan products that do not match beneficiary needs, reducing uptake.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy the real‑time interaction platform, conduct social audits, and integrate feedback into product design.
gen_risks.evidence: Citizen Engagement (CE) will include real‑time platform, participatory monitoring, and grievance redress mechanisms.

gen_risks.description: Private sector may de‑risk by withdrawing lending from non‑flood‑affected areas, limiting overall financial inclusion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design CRF to also provide liquidity for medium‑size shocks and maintain incentives for private lenders in unaffected regions.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF only supports large/extreme shocks; small/medium shocks are retained by private sector.

gen_risks.description: Agritech companies selected through AFIC may under‑perform, reducing the effectiveness of climate‑smart loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear performance metrics, conduct regular audits of ATC services, and tie continued funding to demonstrated outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: AFIC will select 5‑6 ATCs; loans bundled with ATC advisory support to boost yields and resilience.

gen_risks.description: Changes in Government of Pakistan priorities or budget allocations could jeopardise long‑term CRF sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year legislative commitments, embed CRF provisions in national finance law, and diversify funding sources.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF trust owned by GoP; additional financing subject to GoP and WB Board approvals.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private capital mobilisation despite guarantee structures may limit the scale of liquidity available to MFPs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align guarantee terms with market appetite, coordinate with ADB/IFC for co‑financing, and promote private sector participation through risk‑sharing incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: Future guarantee facility with IFC envisaged to leverage IDA resources and complement ADB de‑risking.

gen_risks.description: Market‑based KIBOR pricing of CRF liquidity could make loans unaffordable for vulnerable borrowers, especially women.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer concessional rates or subsidies for women and flood‑affected borrowers, funded by the GSFF grant portion.
gen_risks.evidence: Market terms defined as 6‑month KIBOR; higher borrowing cost imposed if gender allocation deviates.

gen_risks.description: Risk of fraud or misuse of CRF resources due to weak internal controls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement segregation of pooled and child accounts, conduct regular internal audits, and ensure external audit by Auditor General.
gen_risks.evidence: Internal audit department responsible for project audit; external audit by Auditor General of Pakistan.

gen_risks.description: Parametric trigger thresholds may not reflect actual on‑ground damage, causing delayed or inappropriate payouts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use multiple data sources, calibrate triggers with historical loss data, and incorporate post‑event loss calculations for verification.
gen_risks.evidence: Two independent triggers: government emergency declaration or portfolio impact; insurance back‑stop trigger based on sector‑wide portfolio loss.

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is Substantial. The political context in Pakistan remains fluid. However, there has been significant decline in political uncertainty and associated policy instability in recent months, especially in the backdrop of the general elections. Given that a new government took the helm recently and the fact that policy priorities are still being defined, political risks, in particular in the context of the project, remain substantial.
gt_risks.mitigation: In the implementation stage, the risks will be mitigated through frequent monitoring and oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is High. While fiscal consolidation measures have supported short-term stabilization, macroeconomic risks remain high amid a high debt burden (72 percent of GDP), heavy financial sector exposure to government debt, large external financing needs, weak confidence, and little progress with structural reforms. Significant risks include potential worsening of external conditions, further natural disasters, and a slowdown or reversals in policy adjustment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Risks are partly mitigated by government commitment to implementation of reforms under the ongoing International Monetary Fund program, World Bank support to structural policy reforms in the fiscal and power sectors, strong government commitment to the reforms supported by the operation, and the availability of dedicated World Bank technical assistance to implement key reforms.
